title: Putting It Together - Who Has What?
description: Combine everything you've learned: 'He has it', 'Is that yours?', 'It's theirs' - real French!
can_do: Combine object pronouns and possessives in sentences
Say 'He has it', 'I want it', 'It's mine' naturally
Form complex sentences with movement, possession, and objects

concepts.definition: Combine subject + verb + object/possessive to make real sentences
concepts.example: Use everything from previous 9 modules together!

concepts.definition: Object pronouns go BEFORE the verb in French (opposite of English!)
concepts.example: English: 'I see IT', French: 'I IT see' - pronoun comes first

concepts.definition: Multiple ways to express ownership in French
concepts.example: Choose between possessive adjectives and possessive pronouns

items.situation: Someone asks about an object. Confirm the person possesses it
items.hint: Object pronoun goes BEFORE verb. Use contracted form with apostrophe

mistakes.feedback: Object pronoun goes BEFORE verb: il L'a
Use object pronoun, not ça here

items.situation: Confirm a woman possesses something concisely
items.hint: Same pattern - object pronoun before verb

items.situation: A group possesses multiple objects. Use pronouns for both
Someone asks whose book it is. Claim ownership of it (masculine)
items.hint: Use possessive pronoun (not adjective) with article

items.situation: Identify ownership of something belonging to him/her (masculine thing)
items.hint: Possessive pronoun for his/her with masculine article

items.situation: Identify something as belonging to a group (masculine thing)
items.hint: Possessive pronoun for 'their' with masculine article

items.situation: Ask a friend if something belongs to them (masculine thing)
items.hint: Question form: est-ce + possessive pronoun (informal, masculine)

mistakes.feedback: For questions, use: est-ce (not c'est). However, it is OK to use in spoken french

items.situation: Ask if something belongs to a third person (masculine thing)
items.hint: Question form: est-ce + possessive pronoun for his/her

mistakes.feedback: For questions, use: est-ce (not c'est). However, it is OK to use in spoken french

items.situation: Ask if something belongs to a third person (feminine thing)
items.hint: Question form: est-ce possessive pronoun for his/her

mistakes.feedback: For questions, use: est-ce (not c'est). However, it is OK to use in spoken french

items.situation: Say you want something using object pronoun (vouloir + object)

mistakes.feedback: Object pronoun goes BEFORE: je LE veux
Object pronoun goes BEFORE: je LE veux
Use object pronoun '{le}' or '{la}', not ça

items.situation: Tell your friend to come with you (venir + preposition)
Say he's going to leave (aller + infinitive)

mistakes.feedback: Use '{va partir}' to express future intention
